guarantees.claim: On asynchronous reset (negedge rst_ni), sw_key_data_reg[1] is driven to all zeros.
When engine_stable is high and reg2hw.key_share1[j].qe is true, the 32-bit word at sw_key_data_reg[1][32*j+:32] is assigned the value reg2hw.key_share1[j].q; otherwise no update occurs for that word.
When rst_ni is high and engine_stable is low, sw_key_data_reg[1] retains its previous value (no update).

assumptions.claim: Parameter MaxKeyLen is expected to be a multiple of 32 to ensure the loop covers the entire key length without truncation.
assumptions.risk: If MaxKeyLen is not a multiple of 32, trailing key bits are not loaded into sw_key_data_reg[1], potentially leaving residue or incomplete key material.

assumptions.claim: The reg2hw.key_share1 array must have at least MaxKeyLen/32 entries, matching the loop bound.
assumptions.risk: Out-of-bounds access could cause simulation/synthesis mismatch or silent data corruption.

assumptions.claim: The engine_stable signal is asserted only when the engine is in a state ready to accept a new key load and will not use the key until the load is complete.
assumptions.risk: If engine_stable is asserted prematurely or deasserted during partial update, the key register may contain a mixture of old and new key words, leading to incorrect or weak key material.

assumptions.claim: The reg2hw.key_share1[j].qe signal is a pulse or single-cycle strobe that is deasserted after the corresponding q word is loaded; it must not remain high across multiple clock edges without intention to reload the same word.
assumptions.cond: after qe is sampled high and the word is transferred
assumptions.risk: Persistent qe could cause unintended successive overwrites of the same key word, possibly with new values if q changes, resulting in unwanted key modifications.

uncertain_points.claim: The block allows partial updates of sw_key_data_reg[1] (only words with qe high). It is unclear whether the design intends to enforce atomic full-key updates; a partial update could leave a mixture of old and new key words, potentially weakening the key or allowing side-channel leakage.
uncertain_points.cond: engine_stable high and only a subset of qe bits are set
uncertain_points.risk: If the key is used immediately after such a partial load, the resulting key may be insecure.

uncertain_points.claim: MaxKeyLen not being a multiple of 32 would cause the loop bound MaxKeyLen/32 to truncate, omitting the last partial word from being loaded. It is unclear if MaxKeyLen is constrained to multiples of 32 elsewhere.
uncertain_points.cond: Parameter MaxKeyLen set to a non-multiple of 32
uncertain_points.risk: Missing bits can cause incomplete key material, leading to incorrect operation or residue of previous key.

uncertain_points.claim: sw_key_data_reg[1] is only one share of the key. The other share (e.g., key_share0) is loaded separately. There is no indication of coordination between shares; loading them independently could break the secrecy property if one share is updated while the other is not.
uncertain_points.risk: Mismatched shares may leak secret information or render the key invalid.

uncertain_points.claim: The block provides only reset clearing of sw_key_data_reg[1]; there is no fault detection or error-triggered clearing (e.g., on parity error or tamper alert). The key may persist in the register after a fault or deactivation.
uncertain_points.cond: post-reset operation, no explicit key clearing condition besides reset
uncertain_points.risk: Key material may remain accessible to downstream logic longer than intended, increasing exposure window.
